development: AI scribes / ambient clinical documentation
definition: Speech-to-text and LLM tools that listen to clinical encounters and draft visit notes for clinician review, reducing documentation burden.

development: AI-enabled medical imaging devices (regulatory-cleared)
definition: Radiology and other diagnostic software cleared by regulators such as the FDA, with detection and triage algorithms embedded in clinical workflows.

development: AI voice agents for patient access and scheduling (via MHRS public deployment)
definition: Conversational agents handling appointment booking, reminders and care navigation for patients, replacing parts of call-centre and front-desk work.

development: AI-accelerated drug discovery and trial design
definition: Generative and predictive models used to design molecules, select targets and optimise clinical-trial recruitment or protocols.

development: Agentic AI for fraud detection and AML
definition: Autonomous agent systems that monitor transaction signals, draft fraud rules and triage alerts in banks.

development: AI credit scoring and underwriting with alternative data
definition: Machine-learning models that assess creditworthiness from transaction and non-traditional data, extending or automating lending decisions.

development: Agentic commerce and agent-initiated payments
definition: Card-network and fintech protocols, such as Visa Trusted Agent Protocol and Mastercard Agent Pay, letting AI agents authenticate and pay on users' behalf.

development: AI tutors and pedagogically guided chatbots
definition: Generative AI tutoring tools designed with learning principles, offering hints and feedback rather than direct answers.

development: Assessment redesign and integrity policy for generative AI in schools and universities
definition: Widespread student use of generative AI prompting institutions to redesign assignments, exams and academic-integrity policy.

development: AI assistants for teachers (lesson planning, feedback)
definition: Tools that generate lesson plans, materials and marking feedback, now used by a growing share of lower-secondary teachers.

development: Government AI assistants and citizen-service chatbots
definition: LLM-based assistants for frontline public services and internal civil-service work, such as drafting, search and case handling.

development: AI for public-sector decision support and case triage
definition: Algorithmic tools prioritising benefits, tax, inspection or permit cases, requiring audit, transparency and human-oversight arrangements.

development: Agentic AI in government workflows
definition: Autonomous AI agents performing multi-step administrative processes in public bodies, with most agencies planning pilots within two to three years.

development: GeoAI and satellite-based crop monitoring and yield prediction
definition: Foundation models and remote sensing used to map soils, track crop condition and forecast yields at field to national scale.

development: AI advisory chatbots for farmers
definition: Multilingual conversational advisory services giving smallholders agronomic, weather and market guidance tailored to local context.

development: Precision spraying and autonomous farm machinery
definition: Vision-guided sprayers, weeders and autonomous tractors that apply inputs per plant or per zone to cut chemical and fuel use.

development: AI for grid forecasting, fault detection and outage response
definition: Machine-learning tools forecasting renewable output and demand, and detecting grid faults to improve reliability.

development: Data-centre flexibility and demand response
definition: Operating AI data centres to shift or curtail load in response to grid conditions, easing system stress.

development: AI-driven building and industrial energy optimisation
definition: Software that optimises HVAC, process loads and storage dispatch to cut energy use and cost.

development: AI-enabled industrial robots and cobots
definition: Robots using machine learning for perception and adaptation in high-mix, low-volume production, with record global installations.

development: Humanoid and general-purpose robots
definition: Bipedal or general-purpose robots targeting factory and logistics tasks, with roughly 7,000 full-size units sold in 2025.

development: AI predictive maintenance and visual quality inspection
definition: Sensor and computer-vision models that predict machine failures and detect product defects on production lines.

development: Warehouse robotics and automated fulfilment
definition: Fleets of mobile and manipulator robots, with agentic AI coordination, handling picking, sorting and unloading in fulfilment centres.

development: Autonomous trucking
definition: Driverless heavy trucks operating on public highways for commercial freight, currently in the US and China.

development: AI route optimisation and demand forecasting
definition: Machine-learning planners that optimise delivery routes, inventory and capacity, and automate last-mile operations.

development: Generative AI content production (text, image, video, audio)
definition: Use of generative models to create, localise and edit media content at lower cost, including synthetic video and voice.

development: AI answer engines and chatbots as news gateways
definition: Chatbots and AI search summaries replacing direct visits to publisher sites, with weekly chatbot news use rising from 7 to 10 percent.

development: AI content licensing deals between publishers and AI firms
definition: Commercial agreements granting AI developers access to news archives in exchange for payment or attribution.

development: AI content provenance, watermarking and labelling (C2PA, SynthID, AI Act Art. 50)
definition: Obligations to label AI-generated content and deepfakes, such as EU AI Act Article 50, applying from August 2026.

development: Generative legal AI for drafting, research and contract review
definition: Enterprise tools such as Harvey that automate drafting, due diligence and review, with tens of thousands of custom agents.

development: Court and legal-aid AI (e-discovery, case summarisation, access to justice)
definition: Tools used by courts and legal-aid bodies to summarise filings, support research and widen access to legal help.

development: AI personalisation and dynamic pricing
definition: Recommendation and pricing models adapting offers and prices to individual customers or real-time demand.

development: Generative AI customer service agents
definition: LLM-powered chat and voice agents resolving customer queries and returns, replacing parts of call-centre work.

development: New AI roles: AI/ML specialists, AI-agent builders and AI governance
definition: Fast-growing roles in AI and machine learning, big data and AI-tool design, with most firms planning to hire AI-skilled staff.

development: Declining clerical and routine cognitive roles
definition: Roles such as cashiers, ticketing clerks, administrative assistants and some accounting tasks projected to shrink as AI automates routine work.

development: AI-enabled freelancing and AI-implementation micro-agencies
definition: Solo and small-firm services that build or run AI workflows for clients, alongside AI-enabled freelancing platforms.

development: EU AI Act compliance obligations reaching Turkish providers and exporters (extraterritorial scope, staged deadlines)
definition: Staged application of the EU AI Act, with high-risk obligations postponed to December 2027 and August 2028 under the Omnibus.

development: Turkish-language and sovereign LLMs, largely built on open-weight base models
definition: National or language-specific foundation models, such as TÜBİTAK Bilge and HAVELSAN models in Türkiye, reducing dependence on foreign providers.

development: Enterprise agentic AI systems
definition: Autonomous multi-step AI agents deployed in IT, knowledge management and operations, with 23 percent of surveyed firms scaling agents.

development: AI compute and data-centre buildout
definition: Rapid growth in AI data-centre capacity and national supercomputing, such as Türkiye's ARF, with rising power demand.

development: AI-enabled cyber offence and AI-driven cyber defence
definition: Attackers use LLMs and agents for phishing, malware and vulnerability discovery, and defenders answer with AI-automated security operations (SOC triage, threat hunting).

development: Deepfake and voice-clone fraud, and AI-based identity verification (eKYC liveness)
definition: Generative impersonation of customers and executives, with banks answering through AI liveness and deepfake detection in remote onboarding.

development: AI in insurance underwriting and claims, including satellite-based agricultural loss assessment
definition: Computer vision and remote sensing used to price risk and settle claims (motor damage photos, parametric satellite crop loss).

development: AI-driven irrigation scheduling and agricultural water management
definition: Sensor, satellite-evapotranspiration and ML models that schedule irrigation and allocate water at farm and basin scale.

development: AI for disaster risk and rapid damage assessment
definition: Satellite, SAR, drone and ML for post-event building-damage mapping, plus seismic and flood early warning.

development: Secondary use of national health data for AI (EHDS-type health data spaces)
definition: Governed reuse of national electronic health records for training and validating clinical AI under EU health data space regulation.

development: AI literacy and workforce reskilling programmes
definition: Employer and state training to give staff working AI skills, made a legal duty for AI deployers by EU AI Act Art. 4.

development: Algorithmic management and AI in hiring/HR
definition: AI CV screening, interview scoring, scheduling and worker monitoring, classed high-risk under AI Act Annex III.

development: Passive acoustic monitoring with AI species classifiers
definition: Autonomous audio recorders paired with pretrained deep-learning models that detect and identify birds, amphibians, mammals and insects from soundscapes at scale.
named_examples: BirdNET; Perch (Google DeepMind); PNW-Cnet

development: Camera-trap image analysis with AI detectors and species classifiers
definition: Automated detection of animals, people and vehicles in camera-trap images, followed by species-level classification and shared cloud analysis.
named_examples: MegaDetector; SpeciesNet (Google); Wildlife Insights

development: eDNA metabarcoding with ML-assisted bioinformatics, reference-gap filling and portfolio nature-risk analytics
definition: Species detection from water, soil or air DNA samples, increasingly combined with machine-learning ordination and AI-driven site-portfolio nature-risk assessment.
named_examples: NatureMetrics

development: Deep-learning wetland and habitat mapping from Sentinel-1/2
definition: Semantic-segmentation models on Sentinel-1/2 imagery to map wetland types, vegetation and change for conservation and restoration monitoring.
named_examples: Google Earth Engine, Copernicus HRL Water & Wetness, JRC Global Surface Water, Dynamic World

development: Geospatial foundation models for Earth observation
definition: Large pretrained models on multi-sensor satellite archives that are fine-tuned for land cover, habitat, flood or vegetation tasks with little labelled data.
named_examples: Prithvi-EO-2.0 (NASA/IBM); TerraMind (ESA/IBM/Jülich); AlphaEarth Foundations; Clay

development: Digital MRV of restoration outcomes (carbon, wetland extent, vegetation, biodiversity)
definition: Satellite, drone and machine-learning measurement, reporting and verification of restoration outcomes such as tree counts and carbon stock. Includes restoration prioritisation and site-selection via habitat suitability models.
named_examples: Verra and Pachama digital MRV pilot; WRI TerraFund MRV guidance; Restor; GBIF + ML SDMs

development: AI and data tooling for nature-related disclosure (TNFD LEAP, ESRS E4, ISSB nature work)
definition: Software and datasets that help firms and financial institutions locate, evaluate and report nature dependencies and impacts under voluntary and mandatory frameworks.
named_examples: TNFD LEAP approach; ENCORE; WWF Biodiversity Risk Filter; Clarity AI TNFD solution

development: EO/AI-based biodiversity and restoration monitoring for EU reporting (NRR plans, Copernicus indicators, Biodiversa+ monitoring, EuropaBON, BioDT/DestinE digital twins)
definition: Member-state restoration plans due 1 September 2026, with spatial data and indicator monitoring partly pre-filled from Copernicus and EU nature-reporting datasets.
named_examples: EU Nature Restoration Regulation; Copernicus Land Monitoring Service

development: AI research assistants for literature discovery and synthesis
definition: LLM-based tools that search large paper corpora, summarise findings and extract structured evidence tables from natural-language research questions.
named_examples: Elicit; Consensus; Undermind

development: LLM-assisted screening and data extraction in systematic reviews
definition: Human-in-the-loop use of LLMs for title/abstract screening and data extraction, with reported workload reductions but variable accuracy on numerical outcomes.
named_examples: Elicit Systematic Review; Claude and GPT-4 extraction evaluations (Research Synthesis Methods)

development: AI-maintained living evidence databases for conservation decisions
definition: LLM pipelines that screen and classify conservation literature and answer questions on intervention effectiveness from curated evidence databases.
named_examples: Conservation Evidence (University of Cambridge); Imperial College AI evidence pipeline

development: Agentic coding assistants for researcher data analysis
definition: Terminal-based coding agents and integrated AI workbenches that run analysis pipelines end to end for researchers who do not code manually.
named_examples: Claude Code; OpenAI Codex CLI; Claude Science

development: Publisher, funder and university rules on generative AI in research (authoring, peer review, grant applications)
definition: Governance policies from publishers, funders and universities restricting or conditioning use of generative AI in research, peer review and applications.
named_examples: Elsevier generative AI policy; Springer Nature reviewer guidance; NIH notice NOT-OD-23-149

development: Research-integrity screening for paper mills and fabricated content
definition: Automated detection of tortured phrases, reused images, paper-mill patterns and hallucinated references in submitted or published papers.
named_examples: Problematic Paper Screener; Clear Skies Papermill Alarm; STM Integrity Hub

development: AI-assisted citizen-science species identification platforms
definition: Mobile platforms where computer-vision models propose species identifications that communities verify, producing open biodiversity records.
named_examples: iNaturalist; Pl@ntNet

development: Generative AI in grant writing and in funder-side screening
definition: Nonprofits use LLM assistants to draft proposals and reports, while funders are still divided on accepting AI-generated applications.
named_examples: Candid foundation survey; Google.org nonprofit survey; Instrumentl grant-writing AI report

development: Internal generative AI assistants for municipal staff
definition: Self-hosted or governed chat assistants that help city officials draft, summarise and analyse documents without sending data to model training.
named_examples: ChatAmsterdam (Gemeente Amsterdam)

development: AI chatbots and virtual assistants for municipal citizen services
definition: Conversational assistants embedded in city apps and municipal software to answer resident enquiries, including pilots in Turkish municipalities.
named_examples: Istanbul Metropolitan Municipality assistant on Istanbul Senin; BICSA for BELSIS.NET

development: Tech-for-good intermediaries and skills-based AI volunteering for NGOs
definition: Volunteer data scientists and AI engineers working with NGOs on predictive analytics and satellite-based projects, building capacity without in-house staff.
named_examples: DataKind

development: Evidence-to-policy brief generation from scientific literature
definition: Databases that trace where research is cited in policy documents, and LLM methods that turn scientific papers into policy briefs for evidence-informed advocacy.
named_examples: Overton; Sci2Pol benchmark

development: UAV / drone vegetation and habitat mapping with deep learning
definition: Multispectral or RGB drone imagery with segmentation and object-detection models for plant communities, reed beds, nesting colonies.
notes: split from B04 in review 1; needs source

development: Biodiversity / nature credit markets with digital MRV
definition: Tradeable or claimable units for measured biodiversity gain or restoration outcome, verified through remote sensing, acoustics, eDNA.

development: Multi-agent and autonomous AI research systems ("AI co-scientists")
definition: Orchestrated agent teams that generate hypotheses, run analyses, and draft and critique outputs with limited human steps.

development: LLM analysis of public consultations and participatory input
definition: LLMs cluster and summarise citizen submissions, survey answers and deliberation transcripts for municipalities and NGOs.

development: AI urban-nature and climate-adaptation mapping and local digital twins for municipalities
definition: Tree-canopy, green-infrastructure, heat-island and flood models built on EO plus AI, packaged as municipal digital twins.
